facts.statement: Fossils of Opisthodactylus date from the Early to Late Miocene epochs.
This extinct bird lived in the Santa Cruz, Chichinales, and Andalhuala Formations of Argentina.
facts.quote: Opisthodactylus is an extinct genus of rheiform bird from the Early to Middle Miocene Santa Cruz and Chichinales Formations and the Late Miocene (Montehermosan) Andalhuala Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: Three species of Opisthodactylus have been described, including the type species O. patagonicus.
facts.quote: Three species are described: the type species, O. patagonicus, O. kirchneri and O. horacioperezi.

facts.statement: The species O. kirchneri was formally described in 2017 by Noriega and colleagues.
facts.quote: The species O. kirchneri was described in 2017 by Noriega et al.

facts.statement: Fossils of O. horacioperezi were discovered in association with fossils of the giant ground sloth Patagorhacos terrificus.
facts.quote: Fossils of O. horacioperezi were found together with fossils of Patagorhacos terrificus.

facts.statement: Opisthodactylus is classified within the family Rheidae.
Opisthodactylus is an extinct genus of ñandú (rhea) from the Miocene of Argentina.
facts.quote: Opisthodactylus es un género extinto de ñandú del Mioceno de Argentina.

facts.statement: The time range for Opisthodactylus spans from the Aquitanian to the Piacenzian, approximately 21 to 3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aquitanian to Piacenzian (21 to 3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus Opisthodactylus was first described by Ameghino in 1891.
